gt_root_cause: After a GPU hardware failure (NVLink/C2C link loss or GHES GPU containment), the NVIDIA RM driver runs cleanup from nvidia_close. That path goes through gvaspaceInvalidateTlb_IMPL -> kgmmuInvalidateTlb_GM107 -> kgmmuCheckPendingInvalidates_TU102, which polls GPU MMIO registers in a loop. It does not first check whether the GPU is lost or needs a reset, so each MMIO read to the dead GPU (gpuSanityCheckRegRead_IMPL) stalls on ARM64 Grace systems.

gt_root_cause: In drivers/char/ipmi/ipmi_msghandler.c smi_work(), when intf->handlers->sender() returns an error (possible since 9cf93a8fa9513 "ipmi: Allow an SMI sender to return an error"), the error path calls deliver_err_response() and does goto restart without clearing intf->curr_msg or freeing/NULLing newmsg. gt_root_cause: When qgroups are enabled, __btrfs_qgroup_release_data() and qgroup_free_reserved_data() pass an extent_changeset to btrfs_clear_record_extent_bits(). Under the extent io tree spinlock, add_extent_changeset() calls ulist_add() with GFP_ATOMIC for every changed range, even though these callers only read bytes_changed. If that allocation fails under memory pressure, the error reaches BUG_ON(ret < 0) in clear_state_bit() (fs/btrfs/extent-io-tree.c).

gt_root_cause: In the NVIDIA UVM driver, handle_fault() in uvm_populate_pageable.c (called from uvm_populate_pageable_vma(), reached through the UVM_POPULATE_PAGEABLE ioctl) calls handle_mm_fault() once per page in a tight loop that never calls cond_resched(). gt_root_cause: find_first_inode_to_shrink() (fs/btrfs/extent_map.c, the extent-map shrinker) and btrfs_find_first_inode() (fs/btrfs/inode.c) hold root->inodes.xa_lock while scanning the inode xarray, and use cond_resched_lock() to share it. With PREEMPT_NONE, cond_resched_lock() drops the lock only when a reschedule is actually due, so the lock is effectively hogged for long stretches. Other xa_lock users (xa_store in btrfs_add_inode_to_root, btrfs_del_inode_from_root) starve. The unfair test-and-set virt_spin_lock used in KVM guests without PV qspinlocks makes the starvation worse.

gt_root_cause: The Meta x86 kernel configs (facebook/config/common.config and the flavor-*-x86_64.config files) set "# CONFIG_PARAVIRT_SPINLOCKS is not set". On KVM guests, virt_spin_lock_key therefore makes queued_spin_lock_slowpath fall back to the unfair test-and-set virt_spin_lock() loop, which never yields to the hypervisor. The heavily contended btrfs root->inodes xa_lock is taken by btrfs_del_inode_from_root() during eviction, by inode creation, and by the extent-map shrinker (which holds it too long because it uses cond_resched_lock). Under that contention, and with lock-holder vCPU preemption, one vCPU starves.

gt_root_cause: In btrfs subpage mode (64K pages on ARM64), page reclaim runs btrfs_release_folio() -> clear_folio_extent_mapped() -> btrfs_detach_subpage(), which frees folio->private. __remove_mapping() can then fail because of a concurrent reference, so the folio stays in the page cache without its private data. prealloc_file_extent_cluster() in fs/btrfs/relocation.c gets that folio with filemap_lock_folio() and calls btrfs_subpage_clear_uptodate() without first calling set_folio_extent_mapped() to rebuild the private state.

gt_root_cause: Most likely cause: the NVIDIA GB300 GPU on Grace (Clemente/Catalina) does not complete an ATC_INV (ATS invalidation) command. The out-of-tree nvidia-uvm handle_fault() calls handle_mm_fault() per page. That reaches __ptep_set_access_flags(), then __mmu_notifier_arch_invalidate_secondary_tlbs(), then arm_smmu_mm_arch_invalidate_secondary_tlbs() and arm_smmu_atc_inv_domain(), which issues one ATC invalidation per page. arm_smmu_cmdq_issue_cmdlist() then spins with no timeout waiting for the SMMU consumer to move past the stuck ATC_INV. No in-tree fix confirms this cause.

gt_root_cause: __list_lru_walk_one() in mm/list_lru.c holds the per-memcg list_lru_one spinlock for the whole walk and never checks need_resched(). When prune_icache_sb()/super_cache_scan() walks an inode LRU holding millions of inodes on KVM guests, the lock is held for a very long time. Two things make this worse: virt_spin_lock is an unfair test-and-set lock, and the hypervisor can preempt the vCPU that holds the lock. Many direct reclaimers then spin on the same lock.

gt_root_cause: When qgroups are enabled, __btrfs_qgroup_release_data() and qgroup_free_reserved_data() in fs/btrfs/qgroup.c pass an extent_changeset to btrfs_clear_record_extent_bits(). Inside the extent-io-tree spinlock, add_extent_changeset() calls ulist_add() with GFP_ATOMIC to record the range, even though these callers only ever read bytes_changed. Under memory pressure the atomic allocation fails, and clear_state_bit() (fs/btrfs/extent-io-tree.c) hits BUG_ON(ret < 0).

gt_root_cause: When qgroups are enabled, __btrfs_qgroup_release_data() and qgroup_free_reserved_data() (fs/btrfs/qgroup.c) pass an extent_changeset to btrfs_clear_record_extent_bits(). Under the extent IO tree spinlock, add_extent_changeset() calls ulist_add() with GFP_ATOMIC to record each changed range, even though these callers only ever read changeset.bytes_changed. Under memory pressure the atomic allocation fails with -ENOMEM.

gt_root_cause: Bot claim, not confirmed: sched_ext_free() in kernel/sched/ext.c takes the rq lock with task_rq_lock() and then calls scx_ops_exit_task(). The only fbk12 btrfs change I could match to that is the logging and error-handling squash merge 0802192c76d0, which has an empty changelog. gt_root_cause: A dirty 4K block inside a 64K-page folio (ARM64 GH200, sector size smaller than page size) reaches writeback with no ordered extent covering it. In 6.13, btrfs_writepage_cow_fixup() only checks the whole-folio ordered flag (folio_test_ordered), so it does not catch the block. submit_one_sector() then gets a HOLE/INLINE extent map (its ASSERTs are compiled out), and alloc_new_bio() in fs/btrfs/extent_io.c finds no ordered extent. It creates a data-write bbio with bbio->ordered=NULL and a bogus disk_bytenr (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFE00, the hole/inline marker rounded to a 512-byte sector). Why the block is left dirty without an ordered extent (a writeback error path, or a folio re-dirtied behind the filesystem's back) is not confirmed.

gt_root_cause: When qgroups are enabled, __btrfs_qgroup_release_data() and qgroup_free_reserved_data() pass an extent_changeset to btrfs_clear_record_extent_bits(). Under the extent IO tree spinlock, add_extent_changeset() calls ulist_add() with GFP_ATOMIC for every changed range, and clear_state_bit() hits BUG_ON(ret < 0) if that allocation fails. Those callers only ever read bytes_changed, so the range ulist allocation is not needed at all. The fix adds extent_changeset_init_bytes_only(), which skips ulist_add for these paths.

gt_root_cause: Bot claim, not confirmed. On ARM64 with 64K pages (Grace Hopper), pageblock_nr_pages is 8192, so set_recommended_min_free_kbytes() in mm/khugepaged.c raises min_free_kbytes to about 17.3GB. Its 5% cap is based on nr_free_buffer_pages(), which counts ZONE_MOVABLE GPU HBM, so the cap never binds and Normal-zone min watermarks reach about 8.4GB per node. A second post on the same MID says something different: about 65GB of unreclaimable slab (zombie memcg). The MID is a generic oom::see_dmesg bucket covering mostly x86 fleets.

gt_root_cause: When qgroups are enabled, __btrfs_qgroup_release_data() (called from alloc_ordered_extent during cow_file_range) and qgroup_free_reserved_data() pass an extent_changeset to btrfs_clear_record_extent_bits(). Under the extent IO tree spinlock, add_extent_changeset() calls ulist_add() with GFP_ATOMIC to record each changed range, even though these callers only need bytes_changed. Under memory pressure the atomic allocation fails with -ENOMEM and clear_state_bit() hits BUG_ON(ret < 0) in fs/btrfs/extent-io-tree.c.

gt_root_cause: In kernel/sched/ext.c, task_unlink_from_dsq() recomputed dsq->first_task with nldsq_next_task() before calling list_del_init() on the task being removed. When the head task of a user (non-builtin) FIFO DSQ was unlinked, the lookup found that same task again, so dsq->first_task was left pointing at a task that was no longer on the DSQ. The lockless peek (scx_bpf_dsq_peek(), added by 44f5c8ec5b9a) then returned this stale task after it had exited and been freed.

gt_root_cause: swap_reclaim_full_clusters(si, force=true), called from the swap_reclaim_work kworker in mm/swapfile.c, sets to_scan = si->inuse_pages / SWAPFILE_CLUSTER, which can be well over 100K clusters. It then loops over them, dropping and retaking the device-wide si->lock (and going through __try_to_reclaim_swap) each time, and never calls cond_resched(). The unbounded, non-yielding loop came in with 5168a68eb78f ("mm, swap: avoid over reclaim of full clusters").

gt_root_cause: In kernel/sched/ext.c, task_unlink_from_dsq() recomputed dsq->first_task with nldsq_next_task(dsq, NULL, false) before calling list_del_init() on the task being removed. For FIFO DSQs the lookup found the same task again, so dsq->first_task was left pointing at a task that was no longer on the DSQ. This bug came in with the lockless-peek commit 6d2a1143787b6 (upstream 44f5c8ec5b9a, "sched_ext: Add lockless peek operation for DSQs"), which was backported into v6.16-fb without its follow-up fix.

gt_root_cause: Contention on the global mount_lock seqlock spinlock during mount-namespace teardown (free_nsproxy->put_mnt_ns->namespace_unlock->mntput_no_expire takes the write lock once per mount). The contention comes from very large mount namespaces and concurrent readers or umounters. On VMs it is made worse by the unfair virt_spin_lock path. There is no confirmed kernel defect.

gt_root_cause: swap_reclaim_full_clusters() in mm/swapfile.c, called with force=true from the swap_reclaim_work kworker, sets to_scan = swap_usage_in_pages(si) (or si->inuse_pages on 6.13) / SWAPFILE_CLUSTER. That can be hundreds of thousands to millions of clusters when swap is large and nearly full. The loop walks the full_clusters list, taking si->lock or the cluster locks on every pass, and never calls cond_resched(). This behavior came in with 5168a68eb78f ("mm, swap: avoid over reclaim of full clusters").

gt_root_cause: In the pre-iomap fuse_readahead() in fs/fuse/file.c, max_pages = min(fc->max_pages, fc->max_read / PAGE_SIZE) comes out as 0 when the FUSE server advertises a max_read smaller than PAGE_SIZE, which is common on arm64 64K-page kernels. That makes cur_pages 0. fuse_io_alloc(NULL, 0) then calls kzalloc(0) and gets ZERO_SIZE_PTR (0x10), and the `!ia->ap.folios` check does not catch it.

gt_root_cause: The crash kernel (6.12.80 LTS, ust/v6.12.80-fb) carries the stable backport 715c263119fd of "iommu/amd: move wait_on_sem() out of spinlock" (upstream d2a0cac10597). That backport left the cmd_sem_val increment (atomic64_add_return) in iommu_completion_wait() outside iommu->lock. Under concurrent TLB invalidations, CMD_COMPL_WAIT commands can therefore be queued out of sequence order, which breaks wait_on_sem()'s monotonic-sequence assumption. wait_on_sem() then spins until LOOP_TIMEOUT and logs "Completion-Wait loop timed out". Upstream 9e249c484128 (backported as fca7aa0264ae) fixes this by moving the sequence allocation under iommu->lock.

gt_root_cause: Meta's x86_64 kernel config (facebook/config/common.config) had CONFIG_PARAVIRT_SPINLOCKS unset. In KVM guests, native_pv_lock_init() (arch/x86/kernel/paravirt.c) therefore turns on virt_spin_lock_key, and queued_spin_lock_slowpath falls back to the unfair test-and-set virt_spin_lock(). On a large devvm, one CPU holds the split PTE lock (wp_page_copy -> ptep_clear_flush) while it waits for a TLB-flush IPI. Dozens of other vCPUs faulting in the same PMD spin on that lock and starve.

This regression came from 5168a68eb78f ("mm, swap: avoid over reclaim of full clusters").

gt_root_cause: In kernel/sched/rt.c, rto_next_cpu() can return the CPU that is currently running rto_push_irq_work_func(). When that CPU is the only one in rd->rto_mask and other CPUs keep calling tell_cpu_to_push() from pull_rt_task(), rd->rto_loop_next keeps getting incremented. The rto_loop/rto_loop_next mismatch makes the search restart, the same CPU is picked again, and irq_work_queue_on() sends it another self-IPI, forever. The bug was introduced by 4bdced5c9a29 ("Simplify the IPI based RT balancing logic").

gt_root_cause: In mm/swapfile.c, swap_reclaim_full_clusters(si, force=true), called from the swap_reclaim_work kworker, sets to_scan = si->inuse_pages / SWAPFILE_CLUSTER. That can be tens of thousands of clusters, and the function walks si->full_clusters, dropping and retaking si->lock for each cluster, without ever calling cond_resched(). The loop comes from commit 5168a68eb78f ("mm, swap: avoid over reclaim of full clusters"). When swap is nearly full and many CPUs contend for si->lock, one work item runs for tens of seconds and never reports an RCU quiescent state.

gt_root_cause: The Meta backport of "btrfs: inhibit extent buffer writeback to prevent COW amplification" (0858a33c1390/af487dafa8f4 on v6.16-fb) records every extent buffer a transaction handle COWs in the per-handle xarray trans->writeback_inhibited_ebs. btrfs_uninhibit_all_eb_writeback() in fs/btrfs/extent_io.c then walks the whole xarray with xa_for_each() in __btrfs_end_transaction(), and that loop never calls cond_resched(). When one handle COWs a huge number of blocks, as btrfs_evict_inode() does while truncating a large file through btrfs_truncate_inode_items(), the xarray grows without limit and the cleanup walk takes an unbounded amount of time.

gt_root_cause: reweight_entity() in kernel/sched/fair.c rescales se->vlag by old_weight/new_weight (rescale_entity) and never clamps it again. On a large weight decrease of a group sched_entity, se->vruntime can therefore drift far below cfs_rq->zero_vruntime. The next __enqueue_entity() then overflows key*weight in __sum_w_vruntime_add(), which trips the WARN_ON_ONCE overflow guard at fair.c:691 and corrupts the avg-vruntime/rb-tree accounting.

gt_root_cause: The Meta-landed backport 0858a33c1390 ("btrfs: inhibit extent buffer writeback to prevent COW amplification") records every extent buffer a transaction handle COWs in a per-handle xarray. At handle end, btrfs_uninhibit_all_eb_writeback() walks that xarray with xa_for_each() inside __btrfs_end_transaction(), and nothing bounds the walk. When one handle COWs a huge number of blocks (inode eviction or truncate of a heavily fragmented file via the btrfs_truncate_inode_items() search_again loop), the walk becomes arbitrarily long and never reschedules.

gt_root_cause: The Meta/upstream writeback-inhibit feature (af487dafa8f4d / upstream f9a48549a15a, "btrfs: inhibit extent buffer writeback to prevent COW amplification") tracked every COW'd extent buffer of a transaction handle in a per-handle xarray. btrfs_uninhibit_all_eb_writeback() (fs/btrfs/extent_io.c), called from __btrfs_end_transaction(), walked that xarray with xa_for_each() with no bound. When a single handle COWs a huge number of blocks (inode eviction or truncate of a heavily fragmented file via btrfs_truncate_inode_items() search_again loops), the walk becomes arbitrarily long.

gt_root_cause: In fs/btrfs/extent_map.c, find_first_inode_to_shrink() (and find_first_inode() in inode.c) take xa_lock(&root->inodes), walk a very large inode xarray, and yield with cond_resched_lock() when they skip inodes. On CONFIG_PREEMPT_NONE, cond_resched_lock() only drops the lock when a reschedule is actually due, which is roughly once per tick or timeslice. As a result the extent-map shrinker keeps the root->inodes lock almost all the time, and other users of that lock (btrfs_create_new_inode, btrfs_del_inode_from_root via evict/kswapd) are starved.

gt_root_cause: Meta's backports of upstream ddf7233fcab6 ("sched/ext: Fix invalid task state transitions on class switch"), 5a6fb3cfc3fb on v6.16-fb and fa00578ddef7 on v6.13-fb, added a tryget_task_struct()/put_task_struct() pair to scx_enable()'s class-switch loop. That loop runs under scx_task_iter_next_locked(), so scx_tasks_lock and the task's rq lock are held with IRQs off. If a concurrent exit (the delayed_put_task_struct RCU callback) drops the other reference, this put_task_struct() drops the last one. That calls __put_task_struct() -> sched_ext_free(), which does spin_lock_irqsave(&scx_tasks_lock) again: an AA self-deadlock.

gt_root_cause: In the v6.16-fb crash kernel, scx_enable()'s READY->ENABLED class-switch loop in kernel/sched/ext.c runs with scx_tasks_lock held (spin_lock_irq, via scx_task_iter_start) plus the task rq lock. For each task it does tryget_task_struct(p) and later put_task_struct(p). If another holder drops its reference in that window, this put_task_struct() is the last one. __put_task_struct() then calls sched_ext_free() (kernel/fork.c:735), which takes scx_tasks_lock again with spin_lock_irqsave, so the CPU deadlocks on a lock it already holds (AA). Upstream b7d4b28db7da replaces the tryget/put pair in that loop with an SCX_TASK_READY check, which removes the put under the lock.

gt_root_cause: find_first_inode_to_shrink() in fs/btrfs/extent_map.c (the extent-map shrinker) and find_first_inode() in fs/btrfs/inode.c hold root->inodes.xa_lock while they walk a large inode xarray. To share the lock they call cond_resched_lock(), but that only drops the lock when a reschedule is actually needed. Under PREEMPT_NONE this is roughly once per timeslice, so in practice the shrinker holds the lock and other users of it starve.

gt_root_cause: reweight_entity() in kernel/sched/fair.c rescales se->vlag by old_weight/new_weight via rescale_entity() and never clamps it back to the per-entity lag limit. After a large weight decrease on a group sched_entity (update_cfs_group), se->vruntime ends up very far below cfs_rq->zero_vruntime. The next __enqueue_entity() then overflows entity_key()*weight, which trips WARN_ON_ONCE in __sum_w_vruntime_add() (fair.c:691) and corrupts the avg_vruntime accounting and rb-tree ordering.

gt_root_cause: This is the bot's claim and nothing has confirmed it. In the second (class-switch) loop of scx_enable() in kernel/sched/ext.c, the code calls tryget_task_struct()/put_task_struct(p) while holding scx_tasks_lock and the task's rq lock. If a concurrently exiting task's last reference is dropped there, __put_task_struct() calls sched_ext_free(), which takes scx_tasks_lock again. The CPU then deadlocks on a lock it already holds (AA), while still holding the rq lock.

gt_root_cause: In btrfs_drop_extent_map_range() (fs/btrfs/extent_map.c), commit f86f7a75e2fb changed the EXTENT_FLAG_LOGGING clearing to act on em->flags rather than the local 'flags' copy, so split extent maps created while the original map is being logged wrongly inherit EXTENT_FLAG_LOGGING. That flag is never cleared on the split. When the extent-map shrinker (btrfs_scan_inode) later removes and frees such a split, btrfs_remove_extent_mapping() skips list_del_init() because of the LOGGING flag, so the map is freed while still linked on the inode's modified_extents list (WARN_ON(!list_empty(&em->list)) in btrfs_free_extent_map, extent_map.c:67), which is a use-after-free.

gt_root_cause: In scx_enable()'s class-switch loop (kernel/sched/ext.c), ddf7233fcab6 / its v6.16-fb backport 5a6fb3cfc3fb added a tryget_task_struct()/put_task_struct() pair. That pair runs while scx_tasks_lock and the task's rq lock are both held. If the task exits at the same time, the loop's put_task_struct() can drop the last reference, and on !PREEMPT_RT that calls __put_task_struct() -> sched_ext_free() right there. sched_ext_free() then does spin_lock_irqsave(&scx_tasks_lock), a lock this CPU already holds, so the CPU deadlocks on itself (AA deadlock).

gt_root_cause: reweight_entity()/rescale_entity() in kernel/sched/fair.c scales se->vlag by old_weight/new_weight when weight drops and never re-clamps it, so vruntime = avruntime - vlag can land arbitrarily far below cfs_rq->zero_vruntime. Group entities reweighted through update_cfs_group() hit this. The next __enqueue_entity() then overflows entity_key()*weight in __sum_w_vruntime_add(), which trips the WARN and corrupts avg_vruntime and rb-tree accounting.

gt_root_cause: This is the bot's claim and is unconfirmed. A Prestissimo/Velox worker leaked about 179K idle openmp_worker threads (nr_threads=185190). Many of its threads call getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) concurrently while threads keep exiting, and each exit in __exit_signal takes a write_seqlock on sig->stats_lock. That exit churn pushes the readers in getrusage() (kernel/sys.c) and thread_group_cputime() (kernel/sched/cputime.c) off the read_seqbegin_or_lock lockless path and onto the exclusive spinlock, which each reader holds with IRQs off while it walks all threads.

gt_root_cause: On 64K-page aarch64 kernels, GUARD_SZ in kernel/bpf/arena.c is smaller than 2*PAGE_SIZE, so bpf_arena_get_kern_vm_start() (kern_vm->addr + GUARD_SZ/2) returns an address that is not page-aligned. arena_map_free() passes that address to apply_to_existing_page_range(), and apply_to_pte_range() steps by PAGE_SIZE until addr == end, which never happens with an unaligned start. The code was introduced by 317460317a02 ("bpf: Introduce bpf_arena.").

gt_root_cause: scx_cgroup_move_task() in kernel/sched/ext.c has WARN_ON_ONCE(!p->scx.cgrp_moving_from). That warning fires falsely on a legitimate css-only cgroup migration: scx_cgroup_can_attach() checks cgroup identity, while cgroup migration moves tasks by css identity (for example, cpu toggled off and on, then a +memory subtree_control write). The WARN runs from sched_move_task() while the task's rq lock is held.

problems: Minor: the claimed root cause names the false WARN_ON_ONCE as the trigger but leaves out the step that turns it into a hard lockup. The record says the WARN printk runs under the sched_move_task() rq lock and goes out through netconsole. A bnxt TX completion then wakes ksoftirqd and takes the same rq lock again, so CPU 157 deadlocks on itself. The NMI fires on CPU 68 in rcu_tasks_trace, which is spinning in cpu_curr_snapshot on that lock. The fix removes the trigger. It does not touch the printk-under-rq-lock deadlock path.

gt_root_cause: scx_cgroup_move_task() in kernel/sched/ext.c has WARN_ON_ONCE(!p->scx.cgrp_moving_from) at line 4354, and it fires falsely. The condition is legitimate during a css-only cgroup migration: cpu css A is stale, cpu css B is current, and a +memory write pulls the cpu controller into the migration. scx_cgroup_can_attach() arms cgrp_moving_from based on cgroup identity, but the migration itself is driven by css identity, so the field can be NULL here. The WARN fires inside sched_move_task() while the rq lock is held.

gt_root_cause: In net/tls/tls_strp.c, tls_strp_read_sock() reloaded the anchor from the TCP receive queue (tls_strp_load_anchor_with_queue) only when strp->stm.full_len == 0. After a partial record was parsed, TCP could collapse or compact the receive queue skbs (tcp_collapse/prune), which freed the skbs that anchor->frag_list still pointed to. tls_strp_check_queue_ok() then walked those stale skbs. The fix makes the code always refresh the queue.

gt_root_cause: In kernel/bpf/arena.c, GUARD_SZ is fixed at 1<<16 (64K), so on CONFIG_PAGE_SIZE_64KB aarch64 kernels (Grace), bpf_arena_get_kern_vm_start() returns kern_vm->addr + GUARD_SZ/2 (0x8000), which is not page-aligned. arena_map_free() then passes that unaligned address to apply_to_existing_page_range().

gt_root_cause: scx_cgroup_move_task() in kernel/sched/ext.c has WARN_ON_ONCE(!p->scx.cgrp_moving_from). gt_root_cause: Slabs in KMALLOC_NORMAL caches get their obj_exts arrays (used for memory allocation profiling and memcg) from KMALLOC_NORMAL caches too, via alloc_slab_obj_exts() and kmalloc_slab(). That lets two caches hold each other's arrays: kmalloc-512 (64 objects x 16 B = 1024 B, served from kmalloc-1k) and kmalloc-1k (32 x 16 B = 512 B, served from kmalloc-512). The defect came in with 4b8736964640 and was only partly fixed by 280ea9c3154b, which handles only the same-size case.

gt_root_cause: Since bea67dcc5eea, zap_pte_range() -> zap_nonpresent_ptes() -> swap_pte_batch() calls lookup_swap_cgroup_id() (mm/swap_cgroup.c) on any non-present PTE that decodes as a swap entry, without first checking it against swap_info[]. On a swapless host swap_cgroup_ctrl[type].map is NULL, and lookup_swap_cgroup_id() passes it to __swap_cgroup_id_lookup() without a NULL check, so a corrupted PTE (here from a PMD that points at phys page 0; nobody found what wrote it) crashes the host at process exit.

fair_test_rationale: The fatal path (swap_pte_batch -> lookup_swap_cgroup_id with no map check) is fully in-tree. problems: The claim relies on the host being swapless, so that swap_cgroup_ctrl[type].map is NULL. Nothing in the record says the host was swapless, and the record's own notes point the other way. They report a do_swap_page refault livelock with 12,593 'Bad swap offset entry' printks. In the crash kernel (0e127f210adc:mm/swapfile.c), both get_swap_device() and _swap_info_get() print Bad_offset only after swap_info[type] resolved to a real si. get_swap_device() also needs a live si->users percpu ref. On a host with no swap device, swap_info[type] is NULL and the message would be 'Bad swap file entry'. A live device means swap_cgroup_swapon() already set ctrl->map non-NULL. So the more likely mechanism is an out-of-range swp_offset on a valid map, and 42507c66bdde / 63b02a9409cb would not stop it: their only change is 'if (unlikely(!ctrl->map)) return 0;'.

The non-canonical #GP does not prove the map was NULL. With offset 0x3fffffffff7ff, the byte offset is (off/2)*4 = 0x7ffffffffeffc. On a NULL map that gives address 0x0007ffffffffeffc. On a typical vmalloc map base (0xffffc90000000000) it wraps to 0x0007c8ffffffeffc. Both addresses are non-canonical, so the signature fits a valid map as well as a NULL one.

The CrashCortex post itself calls 0eec00b2ad6c7 (the same Jose Fernandez patch) 'related_or_similar', not an exact fix. The post's root cause is 'indexes the map with the bogus swp_offset without bounds check', and its proposed fix is a bounds check plus ratelimit, not a NULL check. The QEMU A/B result belongs to that bot patch, not to the landed patch. Calling the landed patch an 'exact_fix' goes beyond the evidence.

gt_root_cause: An unidentified stray 8-byte store overwrote a userspace PMD entry with 0x67 (present|RW|USER|A|D, PFN 0), so the zap walker reads physical page 0 as a PTE table. The garbage PTEs decode as swap entries, and swap_pte_batch() then calls lookup_swap_cgroup_id() (mm/swap_cgroup.c), which indexes swap_cgroup_ctrl[type].map with an out-of-range swp_offset because there is no bounds check. The bug is exposed by bea67dcc5eea. Sibling records link the corruption to vm.mem_profiling=1,compressed, but that link is not proven.

gt_root_cause: In kernel/events/uprobes.c, the HPROBE_LEASED branch of hprobe_expire() calls try_get_uprobe(), which can return NULL when a concurrent uprobe_unregister()/put_uprobe() has already dropped the refcount to 0. It then returns `get ? get_uprobe(uprobe) : uprobe` with no NULL check, so dup_utask() during fork ends up calling get_uprobe(NULL). This bug came in with dd1a7567784e ("uprobes: SRCU-protect uretprobe lifetime (with timeout)").

gt_root_cause: Meta's out-of-upstream patch 6d9bcd83bcfee ("[PRE-UPSTREAM] mm/page_alloc.c: Batch locking in free_pcppages_bulk") makes free_pcppages_bulk() in mm/page_alloc.c drop and re-take zone->lock (spin_lock_irqsave) every 32 pages. When many CPUs are fighting over zone->lock, the drainer has to queue again for every 32-page chunk. So kcompactd's __drain_all_pages() -> drain_pages_zone() -> free_pcppages_bulk() takes an unbounded amount of time on a PREEMPT_NONE kernel. __drain_all_pages() also has no cond_resched(), which is a secondary contributor that was never fixed.

gt_root_cause: The v6.16-fbk6 backport 81edd93d2ee4 ("mm: use per_vma lock for MADV_DONTNEED", upstream a6fde7add78d) lets madvise_dontneed and PT_RECLAIM run under the per-VMA lock only. The backport of the companion fix was missing. In mm/khugepaged.c collapse_huge_page(), check_pmd_still_valid() runs before vma_start_write(), so PT_RECLAIM can free the PTE table and clear the PMD in that window. pmdp_collapse_flush() then returns a none _pmd, pte_offset_map_lock() fails (SCAN_PMD_NULL), and the failure path calls pmd_populate(mm, pmd, pmd_pgtable(_pmd)). That installs a PMD pointing at PFN 0 with _PAGE_TABLE, i.e. the value 0x67.

gt_root_cause: Upstream commit f06bedfa62d5 ("pNFS/flexfiles: don't attempt pnfs on fatal DS errors"), backported to v6.16-fb as 262b304751faa, changed ff_layout_choose_ds_for_read() in fs/nfs/flexfilelayout/flexfilelayout.c to return ERR_PTR instead of NULL. As a result, a failed DS search is treated as success and *best_idx/ds_idx is never written.

gt_root_cause: In kernel/rcu/tree_stall.h, print_other_cpu_stall() (and likewise print_cpu_stall() and the expedited path synchronize_rcu_expedited_wait() in tree_exp.h) decide to stall and call panic_on_rcu_stall() based on a gp_seq sampled before the slow stall report. They never check again whether the grace period has ended. When the report is flushed synchronously through a slow 8250 serial console, the grace period can finish partway through, and the kernel then panics on a stall that is already over. csd_lock_wait_toolong's synchronous printk storm makes the report take longer, which widens the window.

gt_root_cause: In v6.16-fb scx_enable() (kernel/sched/ext.c), the class-switch loop runs under scx_tasks_lock plus the task's rq lock, taken by scx_task_iter_next_locked(). It does tryget_task_struct(p) and then put_task_struct(p). If a dying task's last reference is dropped at the same moment, the loop's put_task_struct() is the final put. It then calls __put_task_struct() -> sched_ext_free(), which does spin_lock_irqsave(&scx_tasks_lock) again. The CPU is already holding that lock, so it deadlocks on itself (AA) with IRQs off.

gt_root_cause: In the old cgroup-level CFS bandwidth model (kernel/sched/fair.c throttle_cfs_rq()), a throttled cfs_rq such as /system.slice (cpu.max) is dequeued whole, including tasks that were preempted inside kernel critical sections. Here the loguploaderd threads were preempted inside rcu_read_lock() in shrink_slab() during direct reclaim, and they stayed off-CPU for more than 20 s. With CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU and no RCU_BOOST, nothing could force them to run and end the read-side section. The upstream task-based throttle series (v6.18) changes throttling so tasks are only dequeued on return to user space, which means a throttled task no longer holds kernel resources.

exclusion_reason: No landed fix targeting this crash could be found and no human confirmed the diagnosis. The bot's CONFIG_RCU_BOOST fix (f33a15e09deb6 / D118894892) does not exist in the mirror. The upstream task-based CFS throttle series is an older general redesign: it landed in v6.18, a year before the crash, was never backported to 6.12, and its changelog never mentions RCU readers.
gt_root_cause: Per the bot, which no one has confirmed: config commit a323c06fe1bdc ("[kernel] Port preempt settings") set CONFIG_PREEMPT_LAZY=y and unset PREEMPT_NONE. PREEMPT_LAZY does not exist in the 6.12 Kconfig, so the 6.12 build ended up with preemptible RCU and no RCU_BOOST. With that config, throttle_cfs_rq() can dequeue a cgroup (/system.slice, cpu.max) whose task was preempted inside rcu_read_lock() in mem_cgroup_iter() during direct reclaim. The reader cannot run again, so the grace period stays blocked.

gt_root_cause: One PMD entry on a live page table was corrupted to 0x67, with bits 12-63 (the PFN) zeroed, so physical page 0 was treated as a PTE table. Zap then hit a bogus swap entry (type 0, offset 0x3ffffffffffff). zap_nonpresent_ptes() -> swap_pte_batch() (added by bea67dcc5eea) calls lookup_swap_cgroup_id() in mm/swap_cgroup.c without checking the entry against swap_info[] or bounding the offset against the swap_cgroup map size. What produced the PMD corruption is unknown.

gt_root_cause: The v6.16-fb backport of "sched/ext: Fix invalid task state transitions on class switch" (5a6fb3cfc3fb) added tryget_task_struct()/put_task_struct() to the class-switch loop in scx_enable() (kernel/sched/ext.c ~6129-6144). That loop runs with scx_tasks_lock and the rq lock held by scx_task_iter_next_locked(). If a concurrent delayed_put_task_struct() RCU callback drops its reference first, the loop's put_task_struct() becomes the last put. __put_task_struct() then calls sched_ext_free(), which takes spin_lock_irqsave(&scx_tasks_lock) (ext.c:4159) while that lock is already held, so the CPU deadlocks on itself (AA deadlock).

fair_test_rationale: The deadlock can be confirmed from the crash-kernel source alone: put_task_struct() is called under scx_tasks_lock in the scx_enable class-switch loop, and sched_ext_free() takes that same lock. The upstream fix b7d4b28db7da, written by a human maintainer and already on linus-upstream before the crash, removes exactly that put. problems: Check (3) fails for the claimed exact fix b7d4b28db7da. Its changelog does not describe a deadlock, a lockup, or put_task_struct being the last put under scx_tasks_lock. It presents the change as a cleanup: "While tryget_task_struct() does work for this purpose as tasks that fail tryget always will fail it, it's a bit roundabout. A more direct way is testing whether the task is in READY state." The diff removes the put_task_struct(p) from the class-switch loop, which removes the AA path, but that looks like a side effect. Nothing in the changelog ties it to this crash, so calling it 'exact_fix' overstates the evidence.

7900aa699c34 is labelled partial_or_mitigation, but it also removes the AA mechanism completely. It moves sched_ext_free() out of __put_task_struct() and into finish_task_switch() as sched_ext_dead(). Its changelog is about cgroup exit ordering, reported by Dan Schatzberg, and never mentions this deadlock either. So neither fix's changelog describes the crash signature.

There is no human confirmation. human_signal.kind is 'none' and human_comments is empty. All attribution comes from the CrashCortex bot report (high bot confidence) and a cross-reference to MID d115dbf5. Nobody tied these commits to this crash.

The root cause itself checks out against the crash kernel 0e127f210adc. The class-switch loop at ext.c:6129 does tryget and at ext.c:6144 does put_task_struct while holding scx_tasks_lock and the rq lock. The first loop, by contrast, drops the lock before its put. The call path put_task_struct -> __put_task_struct (fork.c:735) -> sched_ext_free -> spin_lock_irqsave(&scx_tasks_lock) (ext.c:4159) exists, and delayed_put_task_struct does call put_task_struct, so the AA deadlock is possible. The fixes (1), the ancestry (2) and the timing (5) all hold. The only reasons for downgrading are the changelogs not matching the mechanism and the lack of human confirmation.
